_comment: Curated, evidence-backed title-convention overrides used ONLY as a last resort by classifyTenureTrackWithEvidence, after every explicit tenure/non-tenure phrase check (stored field, title, description) has come up empty. Each rule fires only for one specific institution's own documented title naming convention -- never a blanket 'this college defaults to X' guess. Add a rule only with a citable, authoritative source (the institution's own faculty affairs / academic tracks page), and keep titlePattern as narrow as the source's own language, so a plain/ambiguous title at that institution still correctly falls through to unclassified rather than being guessed.

rules.college: Columbia University in the City of New York
rules.note: CUIMC's non-tenure track is the 'at CUMC' track: titles in this track carry the academic rank plus the suffix 'at CUMC' (e.g. 'Assistant Professor of Medicine at CUMC'). The unmodified/plain title without that suffix is the Tenure Track, but CUIMC's own docs do not confirm the reverse (plain title => always tenure-track), so this rule is intentionally one-directional and does not attempt to classify plain titles.

Miller School of Medicine's Clinical Educator (non-tenure) track uses 'Professor of Clinical [Department]' / 'Clinical [rank] Professor' titles (e.g. 'Assistant Professor of Clinical - Anesthesiology'), distinct from the Tenure track's unmodified titles. This is also a standard cross-institutional academic-medicine naming convention (Yale, NYU, and others use the same 'Clinical Professor' / 'Professor of Clinical X' pattern for their non-tenure clinician-educator titles), but scoped to this institution only since 'clinical' in a title is not a safe global signal -- some institutions use it loosely for unpaid/volunteer clinical faculty or for tenure-track physician-scientists.

rules.college: The University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston
rules.note: UTMB's own IHOP faculty-titles policy: 'Non-tenure tracks will have a mission designation following the rank: research, instruction, or clinical practice (i.e. Assistant Professor of Clinical Practice).' Matches a rank word (Professor/Professors/Instructor) followed within a short span by one of those three mission designations (also covers the 'Clinic Practice' typo variant seen in the live data), plus the literal 'N-T Trk' (Non-Tenure Track) abbreviation UTMB uses directly in some titles. A plain rank + department title with no mission designation (e.g. 'Assistant Professor, Cardiovascular Medicine') is NOT matched -- UTMB postings don't always state the mission designation, so those correctly stay unclassified rather than being guessed.

SMD Faculty Regulations (PDF) define three distinct non-tenure title series, each confirmed by exact quoted policy language: (1) '[Rank] OF CLINICAL (DEPARTMENT)' e.g. 'Assistant Professor of Clinical Medicine' -- for faculty whose contributions are 'principally clinical or other professional services', explicitly 'not considered academic in the same sense' as the tenure-eligible track; (2) 'CLINICAL [Rank]' prefix e.g. 'Clinical Assistant Professor' -- the Voluntary Clinical Faculty series for unpaid community-based appointments; (3) 'RESEARCH [Rank]' prefix e.g. 'Research Assistant Professor' -- soft-money appointments that 'terminate concurrently with the cessation of the program, grant, or contract.' Deliberately does NOT match a plain 'Assistant Professor'/'Instructor'/'Faculty' title: the regulations state the academic titles for the main (potentially tenure-track) series 'are the same, regardless of the components of professional activity' (Research/Scholarship/Clinical), so a plain title genuinely cannot be resolved from title text alone and correctly stays unclassified.

rules.collegePattern: ^(?:Binghamton University|SUNY Buffalo State University|SUNY Canton|SUNY Cobleskill|SUNY College at Potsdam|SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry|SUNY College of Optometry|SUNY Cortland|SUNY Delhi|SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University|SUNY Maritime College|SUNY Morrisville|SUNY Old Westbury|SUNY Oneonta|SUNY Oswego|SUNY Plattsburgh|SUNY Polytechnic Institute|SUNY Upstate Medical University|SUNY at Fredonia|State University of New York at New Paltz|Stony Brook University|University at Albany|University at Buffalo)$
rules.note: System-wide SUNY HR policy (suny.edu, 'Qualified Academic Rank Titles'): 'Qualified academic ranks are not "tenure track"... By definition, Qualified Academic Rank is: Rank held by those members of the academic staff having titles of lecturer, or titles of academic rank preceded by the designations "clinical" or "visiting" or other similar designations.' ('visiting' is already handled globally by CLEARLY_NON_TENURE_TITLE_RE, so only 'clinical [rank]' and bare 'lecturer' are added here.) Scoped by collegePattern to SUNY's state-operated campuses (university centers, health science centers, and colleges of technology/arts & sciences) that follow this UUP/SUNY-system HR title schema -- deliberately excludes SUNY's separately-governed community colleges (e.g. SUNY Broome, SUNY Onondaga, SUNY Orange, SUNY Westchester, SUNY Jefferson, SUNY Ulster, SUNY Ncc), which have distinct local-sponsor governance and are not confirmed to use the same title schema. The 'clinical' branch allows a wider span after the word so it also matches multi-rank slash chains used heavily at Stony Brook/Buffalo/Downstate postings (e.g. 'Clinical Assistant/Associate/Full Professor') -- an earlier, narrower version that only allowed one optional assistant/associate word missed these entirely.

UK's Office for Faculty Advancement lists its faculty title series and confirms tenure status per series: the Regular/Extension/Special/Librarian series are tenure-eligible, while the Research Title Series (AR 2:5), Clinical Title Series (AR 2:6), and Lecturer Series (AR 2:9) are all explicitly non-tenure-track. Matches the 'Clinical [rank]' and 'Research [rank]' prefix conventions, bare '(Senior) Lecturer', and the literal 'Clinical Title Series' phrase seen directly in one live posting title. Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant, Associate or Professor in/of [Specialty]' title with no series qualifier -- UK posts the large majority of its faculty jobs this way without stating which title series applies, so those correctly stay unclassified rather than being guessed (only 16 of 88 unclassified UK jobs carry an explicit series qualifier).

OSU's faculty appointments policy (trustees.osu.edu bylaws 3335-7) defines three non-tenure 'fixed term contract appointments that do not entail tenure': the Clinical series ('Clinical instructor, assistant clinical professor, associate clinical professor, or clinical professor'), the Teaching series (same pattern), and the Professional practice series (same pattern) -- matching the 'Assistant Professor - Practice' shorthand seen in live posting titles. Separately, OSU's College of Medicine faculty-tracks page defines 'Associated Faculty' as a non-tenure category explicitly including 'Lecturer and Senior Lecturer'. Deliberately does NOT match OSU's very common 'Physician - ... (Open Rank/Track Faculty)' posting pattern (56 of 83 unclassified OSU jobs): 'Open Rank/Track' is OSU's own phrasing that the appointment track is literally undetermined at posting time (could land on tenure-track, Clinical, or Research faculty depending on the candidate) -- genuinely unresolvable from the title, so it correctly stays unclassified rather than being guessed.

rules.college: The University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio
rules.note: UTHSA's IHOP policy (3.1.1 Academic Titles) states only the plain 'Professor, Associate Professor, and Assistant Professor' titles are 'Tenure Titles' -- distinct from the '/Clinical' and '/Research' suffixed titles (see the companion false-valued rule below). Two live postings append an explicit ', Tenure' or 'with Tenure' to the plain title to signal this (e.g. 'Chair and Professor, Tenure'), a positive signal not covered by the shared global TENURE_RE pattern (which requires 'position/appointment/rank/role' to precede 'with tenure', not follow it).

rules.college: The University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio
rules.note: UTHSA's IHOP policy (3.1.1 Academic Titles), quoted directly: 'Professor, Associate Professor, and Assistant Professor are the only academic titles in which faculty members may hold tenure or be on the tenure track.' Non-Tenure Titles are explicitly enumerated: 'Professor/Clinical ... or Professor/Research ...', 'Associate Professor/Clinical ... or Associate Professor/Research ...', 'Assistant Professor/Clinical ... or Assistant Professor/Research ...', 'Instructor/Clinical ... or Instructor/Research ...' (Section A.2.b) -- matching the '[Rank]/Clinical' and '[Rank]/Research' suffix convention seen throughout live posting titles. Section B separately lists 'Other Non-Tenure Titles' including the prefix form ('Clinical Professor, Clinical Associate Professor, Clinical Assistant Professor, Clinical Instructor...'), 'Lecturer'/'Senior Lecturer'/'Distinguished Senior Lecturer', and bare 'Instructor' ('This title denotes a probationary appointment...'). Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant Professor'/'Associate Professor'/'Professor' with no suffix, nor the very common 'Open Rank Faculty ...' postings -- both are the Tenure Titles category or genuinely undetermined, and stay correctly unclassified.

SRJC's own live posting text (quoted directly, verified 2026-09-10 on an 'Associate Faculty - Chemistry' posting): 'Santa Rosa Junior College is currently accepting applications on a continuous basis to establish a pool for associate faculty assignments. Associate assignments may be temporary, part-time and/or on-call... A part-time faculty assignment may not exceed a total of 67% of an annual full-time assignment.' All 70 of SRJC's unclassified postings at the time used the exact title prefix 'Associate Faculty - [Subject]'. Scoped to this one college (not generalized to 'Associate Faculty' at other California community colleges) since only this institution's own posting language was directly verified.

CWU's Faculty Code structurally separates 'academic rank' (professor/associate professor/assistant professor -- the tenure-eligible titles) from 'professional designation' (clinical faculty, senior research associate, research associate, senior lecturer, lecturer, visiting professor, coach) as two distinct faculty categories (Section I.A.1.a). Corroborated by the CWU/United Faculty of Central CBA, which describes Lecturer positions as a non-tenure track faculty category. Matches the dominant 'Lecturer Pool - [Subject]' posting pattern (55 of 65 unclassified CWU jobs) plus the literal 'Nonpermanent' qualifier seen on one posting.

UW's Academic Personnel & Faculty site (ap.washington.edu) documents five professorial tracks: Tenure, 'Without Tenure by reason of funding (WOT)', Research, Teaching, and Clinical Practice -- with 'Tenure status: N/A' listed explicitly for every rank in the last four. WOT specifically means faculty whose salary comes from grants/contracts/clinical revenue rather than state-appropriated funds, so they don't hold tenure even though fully integrated into department activities. Separately, UW's 'Acting Titles' policy page confirms: 'acting faculty appointments do not have implications for the award of tenure or for promotion in a clock-managed rank' (used for ABD candidates and postdocs past the terminal-degree limit, pending conversion to a regular title once the degree is conferred). Matches the '(WOT)' abbreviation, 'of Clinical Practice' suffix, 'Clinical [rank]'/'Clinical Faculty' prefix, 'Teaching/Research [rank]' prefix in either word order, and 'Acting [rank]' prefix. Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant Professor' with no qualifier, nor administrative/dean titles -- both stay correctly unclassified.

USF's Provost office confirms the 'Professor of Instruction Series' (Assistant/Associate/Professor of Instruction) is explicitly for 'full-time, non-tenure track teaching positions', alongside a separate non-tenure 'Instructor Series' (Assistant/Associate/Senior Instructor) -- both referred to collectively as 'instructional faculty'. Matches the 'of Instruction' suffix, 'Instructional Faculty' label, and the 'Instructor I'/'Instructor 1' grade notation seen on several clinical/allied-health (APRN, PA) postings. Also matches the explicit 'Clinical Faculty Position' label used on medical-school postings, consistent with the non-tenure clinical-track convention already verified at every other academic medical center in this table (Miami, UTMB, Rochester, UTHSA, UW), though not independently re-confirmed in USF's own documentation. Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant Professor'/'Open Rank Faculty' posting with no qualifier (26 of 39 unclassified USF jobs) -- correctly stays unclassified.

Weaker evidentiary basis than the other rules in this table -- no explicit written tenure policy was located (search results repeatedly conflated TSTC with the unrelated Texas State University). This rule instead rests on a structural finding, empirically checked against every TSTC posting ever scraped (40 jobs, 28 unique titles): zero contain 'Professor' in any form -- 'Instructor' is the entire title vocabulary. Combined with TSTC's own institutional identity as a state technical/vocational college (welding, HVAC, diesel, electrical lineworker, aviation maintenance, etc., not a research university), 'Instructor' here reads as the sole, terminal job title for this employer rather than an entry pre-tenure rank on an academic ladder. Revisit if a professorial title is ever observed at this college.

UW-Madison's School of Medicine and Public Health (SMPH) defines six faculty tracks: Clinical Health Sciences (CHS), Clinician Teacher (CT), Tenured/Tenure-Track, Research Professor, Teaching Professor, and Clinical Adjunct. Quoted directly: 'UW-Madison only recognizes the tenure track faculty as full faculty members of the university. The other categories of SMPH faculty are considered academic staff according to UW-Madison policies.' Matches the '(CHS)'/'(CT)' abbreviations seen throughout live posting titles (including bare, un-parenthesized forms like 'Professor CHS-Cornea Service'), plus 'Research Professor', 'Teaching Professor'/'Teaching Faculty', and the 'Clinical [rank]' prefix convention. Deliberately does not match a plain 'Assistant Professor' with no track qualifier (9 of 35 unclassified UW-Madison jobs, including several outside the medical school entirely, e.g. Political Science) -- correctly stays unclassified.
